title: Pluggable route validation pipeline and staged safety rollback for policy engine
creator: Arjun Patel
description:
Summary:
Refactor the routing policy engine to support a pluggable validation pipeline that enforces a typed route schema, policy conformance rules, and safe migration controls for staged rollouts. The goal is to make DSL/config validation modular, unit-testable, and safe-to-deploy with automated rollback triggers when a new policy causes regressions or incompatibilities.

Background:
Current validator logic for routing rules is monolithic and intertwined with the dispatcher. This causes risky migrations, slow iteration on schema changes, and poor observability when policies are rejected/fallbacks are engaged. We need a clear separation: parse -> typed schema validation -> semantic checks (region/tier constraints) -> safety heuristics (capacity-aware fallback/auto-rollback).

Deliverables:
- Pluggable validation pipeline (Java/Go library) with well-defined extension points for: syntax parsers, schema validators, semantic rule plugins, and safety heuristics.
- A canonical typed schema (JSON Schema + additional typed constraints) and migration guide for existing policies.
- Staged rollout controller that can apply policy changes to a subset of traffic, monitor for errors/regressions, and automatically rollback when thresholds are exceeded.
- Comprehensive unit and integration tests + a migration tool to convert common legacy rule shapes.
- Confluence spec, example policies, and a demo in the staging cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New pipeline accepts existing policy set after migration with <= 3% manual edits.
2) Policy validation errors are actionable and surfaced in Console with links to failing rule lines.
3) Staged rollout can be configured per-customer and will trigger rollback if error rate increases by >1.5x baseline or latency regresses beyond SLO.
4) No measurable increase in 95th percentile route lookup latency in production (<= 5ms delta).

Non‑goals:
- Rewriting the dispatcher runtime scheduling knobs. This ticket focuses on validation and safety only.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Adding a typed schema increases migration cost for teams with ad-hoc rules; mitigated with a migration tool.
- Pluggable plugins add surface area for bugs; we'll gate third-party plugins behind feature flags and internal reviews.
- Automated rollback introduces risk of flapping; rollout controller will include cooldown windows and manual confirmation gates for high-impact policies.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped core team (Maya, Arjun, Lina - infra, Diego - console). Agreed on modular pipeline approach and using JSON Schema + small typed extensions for constraints. Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/confluence/display/INF/Pluggable+Route+Validation

2026-02-18 - Spike complete: prototype validator implemented in Go. Parser now emits a typed AST; initial semantic tests for region selection and tier affinity pass against sample policies. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-validator/pull/87

2026-02-25 - Design review with PM (Sofia) and Console (Diego). Feedback: make validation errors include 'fix hints' and policy line/char offsets for Console linking. Added an error payload shape accepted by Console-UI.

2026-03-02 - Performance check: local benchmark showed +1.2ms median and +3.8ms p95 for policy validation path when validating on hot-reload. Decided to run validation async on config change and cache validated artifacts for serving to avoid per-request overhead.

2026-03-06 - Safety controller prototype: staged rollout implemented using percent-based traffic mirroring in staging. Automatic rollback logic wired to error-rate and token-latency metrics from telemetry. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.internal/redwood/routing-rollouts
2026-03-09 - Security review request filed. Notes: validation pipeline will not accept dynamic code execution; plugins run in a sandboxed process with limited privileges. Security ticket: SEC-1294
2026-03-10 - PM sign-off on approach; moving to implementation of migration tool and tests. Next PR: add migration CLI and conformance test harness.
